                    1   counsel for the Sewell Defendants replied that “We have a deal in principle. Please draft an

                    2   agreement as soon as you can.”

                    3           The settlement agreement was delayed due to the Holidays and other commitments, but on

                    4   January 12, 2026, Live Oak’s counsel provided a draft forbearance agreement. Since that time,

                    5   Like Oak has worked in good faith to finalize the settlement agreement. However, the revisions

                    6   Live Oak has received are not in compliance with the express and clear terms of the agreement as

                    7   set forth in Live Oak’s November 25, 20225 email.

                    8           On March 5, 2026, counsel for the Sewell Defendants responded to Live Oak’s latest draft

                    9   agreement in which the Sewell Defendants continued to demand terms that were not agreed to.

                 10     Further, the agreement included new demands to the terms of the settlement in direct

                 11     contradiction to the terms set forth in the November 20, 2025 email. After careful consideration,

                 12     on March 13, 2026, Live Oak, through counsel, informed the Sewell Defendants of its position

                 13     regarding these revisions and that, further, it did not believe that settlement was possible at this

                 14     time.

                 15             Live Oak is aware that the Sewells assert that their revisions comply with the Settlement

                 16     Agreement agreed to. Live Oak doubts this Court will decide to inquire into this issue, but Live

                 17     Oak has the receipts, and further, has provided them to counsel for the Sewells with a detailed

                 18     breakdown as to which revisions violate the express language of the agreed settlement. No

                 19     substantive response has been provided to Live Oak. In the unlikely event of any inquiry, Live

                 20     Oak has little doubt it would prevail on this issue.

                 21             On that basis, Live Oak stated it would inform the Court of that settlement has failed and

                 22     requested dates for a deposition of Bret Sewell. The Sewells’ counsel has explicitly refused to

                 23     provide dates, leading Live Oak to notice a deposition on its own accord. The Sewells’ counsel

                 24     has stated they will not appear at that date, nor will they continue to provide dates. As such, a

                 25     motion to compel will be forthcoming. Beyond that, Live Oak requests that the Court (i) place

                 26     the case back on active status; (ii) set new trial deadlines; and (iii) set a hearing on Live Oak’s

                 27     Motion to Strike [Dkt. # 19].

                        1        Pursuant to this Court’s December 15, 2025 order, Defendants Bretton and
                        2 Christine Sewell, in their individual capacities and as Trustees of the Sewell Family

                        3 Trust (the “Sewell Defendants”) provides the following status report as to the

                        4 settlement of this case.

                        5        On September 16, 2025, Live Oak and defendants Bretton and Christine
                        6 Sewell, individually and as Trustees of the Sewell Family Trust (the “Sewells”)

                        7 mediated the matter with Ret. Judge George Hernandez with ADR Services. The

                        8 matter did not settle, but settlement discussions continued in principal.

                        9 Defendants’ Position:
                       10        The parties attended mediation in September of 2025 before Ret. Judge
                       11 George Hernandez and while they did not settle at the mediation session, they

                       12 agreed on a general framework for settlement which included a paydown of the loan

                       13 balances by $1,000,000 by the end of December of 2025 through collection of

                       14 receivables owing to the Trim Tech entities, or cash payment by Mr. and Mrs.

                       15 Sewell, listing of the real property securing the loans by March 1st and close of

                       16 escrow or pay off of the loans by September 30, 2025. The bank agreed not to

                       17 foreclose during the relevant period and the Sewells agreed to a judgment of

                       18 foreclosure if the sale or pay off did not take place. Thereafter, Mr. and Mrs. Sewell

                       19 collected close to $2 million dollars in receivables paying off the line of credit in its

                       20 entirety despite there being no final settlement agreement. All receivable payments

                       21 went directly to Plaintiff because of a loan terms requiring all such payments to be

                       22 sent to the bank after default in September of 2024.

                       23        After numerous back and forth emails between counsel for the parties, and the
                       24 significant pay down of the loan balances, Plaintiff sent terms for a settlement on

                       25 November 20, 2025 on the terms set forth above excluding the $1,000,000 pay down

                       26 which had already taken place by email confirmation on November 20th, 2025. The

                       27 email includes very specific terms and none of them includes a non-litigation

                       28 Forbearance Agreement. Defendants did not agree to the terms in the email but

                        1 rather requested the loan balance information along with an accounting of receivable

                        2 payments and application of the same and a draft agreement. Defendants received a

                        3 partial accounting on December 10th and confirmed a settlement in principle

                        4 pending receipt and approval of a written settlement agreement. Plaintiff’s counsel

                        5 was to draft a settlement agreement. A draft agreement was finally provided by

                        6 Plaintiff’s counsel on January 12, 2026.

                        7        The draft agreement was formatted like a Forbearance Agreement requiring
                        8 Defendants to waive all rights to seek court intervention under any circumstances

                        9 and including incorrect recitations based upon the agreement in principle contained
                       10 in the email exchanges. The agreement was not drafted like a true settlement

                       11 agreement of disputed litigation but rather as a one sided threat giving the bank

                       12 unfettered discretion to declare a default and foreclose for any reason whatsoever

                       13 eviscerating the agreements the bank purported to make in settlement discussions.

                       14 Defendants responded repeatedly by modifying the agreement presented to more

                       15 appropriately model resolution of disputed litigation.

                       16        One of the issues that came up on negotiation of the settlement going back to
                       17 2025 was the bank’s recordation of a lis pendens. The recordation will affect the

                       18 purchase price, the defendants’ broker provided a letter to the bank confirming the

                       19 issue, and after repeated requests and offers to provide some other form of

                       20 “security” to the bank to remove it before listing, the bank steadfastly refused in yet

                       21 another (in a long line) of attempts to prevent Mr. and Mrs. Sewell from paying off

                       22 the loans and preserving as much equity in the home as possible.

                       23        The bank admitted that the property is worth far more than the loan balance.
                       24 The property is the Sewells home which they reside in with their minor children.

                       25 The Sewells invested over $200,000 into improving/updating the property since the

                       26 mediation as they represented to the bank that they would. The property was worth

                       27 approximately $8 to $8.5 million unimproved, which was more than enough to

                       28 cover Plaintiff’s outstanding balance back in September of 2025. The Sewells were

                        1 forced to list the property with the lis pendens because of Plaintiff’s bad faith. It has

                        2 been listed for $11.9 million, far exceeding the balance owed to the bank which is

                        3 $6.3 million.

                        4        Plaintiff’s counsel never provided any explanation as to why the changes to
                        5 the agreement requested by Defendants would prejudice the bank or were contrary

                        6 to law. The response was always, “this is the way we do it”. Plaintiff’s counsel

                        7 emailed Defendants’ counsel on Friday, March 13, 2026 at 3:48 p.m. providing

                        8 notice that the bank was backing out of the settlement, threatening to notice

                        9 depositions of Mr. and Mrs. Sewell and file a summary judgment motion.
                       10        The Sewells intend to continue along the path to sale of the property and seek
                       11 leave to amend to file a cross-claim against the bank for damages resulting from the

                       12 bad faith actions of the bank which have and will result in financial harm to the

                       13 Sewells. The Sewells also intend to seek injunctive relief if necessary requesting

                       14 that the Court order the bank to release the lis pendens and enjoining any foreclosure

                       15 judgment for an appropriate amount of time to allow a sale or pay off to occur.

                       16        Defendants request a Settlement Conference with the Court or Magistrate
                       17 Judge to explore the possibility of getting the bank to do what it originally agreed to

                       18 do given the substantial equity cushion in the property.

                       19        In the alternative, Defendants have no objection to resetting the trial date and
                       20 resetting discovery cut off dates, allowing sufficient time for Defendants to file a

                       21 Motion for Leave to File a Cross-claim against Plaintiff and time for discovery on

                       22 the new pleading.
